states.name: dark
states.gap: No block-level indicator for the blockquote at all: A marks a two-line quote with a single 17px-wide '>' glyph at #7A7A7A (contrast 4.08:1 on #F9F9F9) and nothing else, where B draws a 4px #494949 rule running the full 144px of the quote. A's inline code chip is also nearly invisible — flat #EEEEEE on #F9F9F9 is a delta of 11 grey levels (1.09:1), versus B's #272727 on #1A1A1A at 1.31:1 — and A's caret is #1C1C1C, the exact same ink value as body text, so in a monospace wall it reads as another l/|/I stem instead of a cursor.
states.gapTheirs: B does not hang its markers, so the prose left edge staircases: body paragraph starts at x=673, bullet text at 721, blockquote text at 721, ordered-list text at 747 — 74px (three full 24.5px monospace cells) of raggedness on one screen. Worse, inside a single wrapped blockquote sentence line 1 starts at 721 and line 2 at 676: the text steps 45px LEFT mid-sentence. A puts every block's first character at x=673±2 and right-aligns all six marker types into a gutter ending at x≈647.
states.verdict: A gives you one prose column and puts the syntax outside it; B leaves the syntax in the column and lets it shove the sentences around. You notice B the moment you write a list under a paragraph — the words jog two characters right for no reason a reader will ever see, and a wrapped quote line drops back left mid-thought, which reads as a rendering fault rather than a design. B buys you a findable caret and a quote rule and pays for it with a document that never holds a straight left edge; A buys the straight edge and pays with a code chip you have to hunt for and a caret the same colour as the text. For a long passage, the stable margin wins and it isn't close.
secondary: B uses two different marker greys: #636363 (2.90:1) for #/##/> but #808080 (4.41:1) for - and 1. — the least meaningful markers are 52% louder than the heading markers. A holds #7A7A7A (4.08:1) across all six marker types.

B's inline code chip is two-tone: #272727 body with two 8px-wide #343434 stripes at x1596-1603 and x1756-1763, i.e. an extra background layer painted behind each backtick delimiter. A's chip is one flat #EEEEEE rect from x1572 to x1788 with no seams.

Caret geometry: A 4px x 54px #1C1C1C, sitting clear in the gap (x1906-1909, comma begins x1916). B 6px x 68px #00B5FF — 94% of the 72px line box, 25% of a 24.5px character cell, and butted directly against the following comma at x1918 so the comma is clipped.
B double-marks the blockquote: 4px rule at x644-647 AND the literal '>' glyph at x675-692. Redundant, and the '>' is what pushes the first line out of alignment with the second.
Fenced code block is identical in both: x644-2236, top edge y1728, chip fill #EEEEEE / #272727 respectively.
Inline emphasis is a wash — both render *small thing* and **not moving** with dimmed asterisks and styled text, same weights, same positions.
